passage:
Monday: At the school fair, Sarita sat cross-legged in front of the puppet show, mouth open as the tiger puppet chased the monkey. Her Masi, Himani, walked right past the front row with a tray of lemonade. Sarita didn't blink.
Tuesday: "I waved at you!" said Himani Masi. "No, you didn't come," said Sarita, very sure.
Saturday: At the next show, Masi sat beside Sarita and whispered, "Watch the puppets, but look for me when they bow." When the puppets bowed, Sarita turned and squealed. "You're here!"

qa.q: What was Himani Masi carrying when she walked past?
qa.a: She was carrying a tray of lemonade.

qa.q: Why was Sarita so sure Himani Masi hadn't come?
qa.a: Sarita was so absorbed and delighted by the tiger chasing the monkey that Masi simply didn't register, so she felt truly confident that Masi had not come.

qa.q: What small trick helped on Saturday?
qa.a: Masi sat close and gave a clear moment to look, when the puppets bowed, so Sarita could enjoy the show and still notice her.

qa.q: How might Himani Masi have felt when Sarita said she didn't come?
qa.a: She may have felt a little hurt or puzzled, having walked right past, until she realised Sarita was just deep in the show.

grounding: It shows a preschooler watching a puppet show who misses her aunt walking right past, because attention pulls to one focus.

passage:
The temple fair was loud: drums, bells, a balloon seller shouting. Santosh, five, sat on the mat in front of the puppet stage while his mother, Hansa, searched the nearby steps for his lost sandal, glancing back at him every few seconds.
She found it and walked past the stage waving it, calling his name. His eyes stayed on the king puppet's golden crown. She passed again with a water bottle, right in front of him. Nothing.
When the show ended he turned and saw her. "Amma, you went away!"
"Kanna, I walked past you twice!"
He shook his head, very sure. "No. Only the king was there."

qa.q: What were Santosh's eyes fixed on?
qa.a: His eyes stayed on the king puppet's golden crown.

qa.q: Why was Santosh so sure his mother had gone away?
qa.a: Santosh was so absorbed in the king puppet's golden crown that his mother vanished for him, so he truly felt she had gone away and was upset about it.

qa.q: What could Hansa do at the next busy show?
qa.a: Sit beside him or touch his shoulder when she comes back, instead of expecting him to notice her walking by in the noise.

qa.q: What is it like for Hansa when Santosh says she went away?
qa.a: She is probably surprised and a little amused 😅, since she walked right past him twice while keeping an eye on him.

grounding: It shows a preschooler at a noisy fair who misses his mother walking past twice because his attention is fixed on the puppet show.

passage:
In the colony hall in Chennai, the Sunday puppet show had begun. Sonali, five, sat in the front row as the crow puppet tried to steal the grandmother's vadai.
Behind the rows, her father, Saurabh, walked slowly across the hall carrying a huge red balloon he had bought for her. He even stopped and bounced it near the front. Other children pointed. Sonali didn't turn.
After the show he held out the balloon. "Did you see me walk past?"
Sonali's eyes went wide. "When? You weren't here!"
"I was right there, with this big red thing."
She stared at the balloon as if it had appeared by magic.

qa.q: What was Saurabh carrying across the hall?
qa.a: He was carrying a huge red balloon he had bought for Sonali.

qa.q: Why did Sonali stare at the balloon as if it had appeared by magic?
qa.a: Sonali was surprised and amazed, because her attention had been so fixed on the crow and the vadai that she never saw the balloon until it appeared in front of her.

qa.q: What could Saurabh learn about getting Sonali's attention?
qa.a: When she is deep in something, even a big red balloon may not register; going close and speaking to her directly works better.

qa.q: Why might the other children have noticed Saurabh when Sonali didn't?
qa.a: They weren't as locked onto the puppets at that moment, so the balloon caught their eye, while Sonali's attention had no room left for it.

grounding: It shows a preschooler absorbed in a puppet show who misses her father walking past with a balloon, as attention pulls to one focus.

passage:
"Darshan, did you like the puppet show?"
"Yes, Dadu! The king puppet fell off the horse, and the horse danced!"
"Did you see Mama walk right past you in the middle of it? She was carrying the ice cream."
"No! Mama didn't come."
"She did. She walked in front of the stage and waved."
Darshan frowned. "I was watching the king. I didn't see anything else."
Dadu laughed. "That's how eyes work, little one. When you look hard at one thing, the rest goes away."
"Where's my ice cream, then?"
"Melting, in Mama's hand. Run!"

qa.q: What happened to the king puppet?
qa.a: The king puppet fell off the horse.

qa.q: How did Darshan feel about the puppet show and about missing Mama?
qa.a: Darshan felt excited by the king puppet and the dancing horse, and then surprised and puzzled to hear Mama had walked right past, frowning because nothing else had been noticed.

qa.q: How did Dadu handle Darshan's surprise, and why was that helpful?
qa.a: He laughed kindly and explained that looking hard at one thing makes the rest go away, so Darshan learned it was normal, not a silly mistake.

qa.q: What might Mama have felt when she waved and got no response?
qa.a: She may have been amused, seeing how completely the show had caught Darshan's attention even as she walked in front of the stage.

grounding: A preschooler watching a puppet show misses Mama walking right past, because attention locks onto one focus.

passage:
Teacher's note, KG-A, Friday. Payal
A puppet group visited today. During the story of the clever crow, our principal slowly crossed the back of the hall carrying a tall plant in a red pot. Afterwards I asked Indu, who sat in front, "Did anyone walk past during the show?" Indu said firmly, "No, Ma'am. Only the crow." When I told the class about the principal, Indu's eyes went round. "A PLANT? I didn't see!"
What I did next: we talked about how our eyes follow whatever our mind is busy with. Everyone giggled 😊

qa.q: What was the principal carrying across the hall?
qa.a: A tall plant in a red pot.

qa.q: What do Indu's round eyes suggest when hearing about the principal?
qa.a: They suggest real surprise; Indu had been so wrapped up in the crow that the principal simply wasn't seen.

qa.q: How did Payal turn the surprise into something useful for the class?
qa.a: She talked with them about how eyes follow whatever the mind is busy with, so missing the plant felt interesting rather than embarrassing.

qa.q: What might the principal have thought, walking across and seeing no heads turn?
qa.a: The principal may have been amused, seeing how completely the puppets held the children's attention.

grounding: A teacher notes a preschooler so absorbed in a puppet show that a person crossing the hall with a plant goes unseen.
